messages:
maria: quick brain-dump: experimenting with a small addition to rollout metadata called `epoch_id` + a `grace_policy` enum to make cross-region rollouts less chattery. idea is per-model-family monotonic token issued by control plane. any objections?

zach: curious: how is this different than the `release_epoch` we talked about before? naming nit, but also: do clients race on multiple epochs?

maria: similar concept but slightly different semantics. `epoch_id` is opaque (uuid-ish) + monotonic counter, clients use monotonic compare only if they also advertise "epoch-aware" capability. We avoid counter-only relying on wall-clock.

ana: define `grace_policy` please. i assume it's how resolvers accept transitions?

maria: yea. proposal: `grace_policy` = one of ["soft","hard","sticky"]. semantics: soft-> resolver will prefer newer epoch after `grace_seconds` unless explicit pin; hard-> immediate prefer new epoch; sticky-> keep existing binding for tenants with recent affinity for TTL.

ryan: minor edge: sticky needs a clear TTL and eviction rule. otherwise we create hidden long tails. suggest `sticky_ttl_sec` and telemetry.

tess: SDK impact: clients that don't opt into epoch-aware should ignore fields. for typed SDKs we can add `resolverOptions.epochAware = true|false`. Should we return `epoch_id` in model catalog responses or only resolver-layer?

maria: return in catalog and in per-route rollout metadata. Example snippet: 
```
{"model":"gen-7","rollout": {"epoch_id":"2026-03-22-17-7","epoch_counter":17,"grace_policy":"soft","grace_seconds":120}}
```

zach: sounds fine. Suggest add `precedence_hint` for client-side testing: values like "pin","lease","epoch","default" so telemetry can attribute why resolver chose variant.

ana: on precedence: explicit tenant pin > hard lease > tenant-preferred affinity > epoch policy > default. we should document that order in the schema doc.

ryan: testing plan: matrix for (pin vs lease vs affinity vs epoch) x (soft/hard/sticky) x (old client vs epoch-aware client). i can write unit harness to simulate resolver races and failovers.

maria: i'll draft RFC follow-up with schema + migration steps: mark fields optional, feature-flag rollout, SDK change notes, migration tests. will include backward compat guidance: older clients ignore unknown fields by default.

infra-bot: infra: feature-flag `epoch-rollout` turned ON in staging: us-west-2 at 2026-03-22T17:22:01Z :gear:

tess: ops note: when enabling in prod, we should gate by catalog consistency checks. a stale catalog could have lower epoch and cause sticky clients to regress. add reconcile job to watch increasing epoch monotonicity.

zach: good point. also we should have a short-circuit: if epoch_counter jumps by > 100 in < 1min, alert. could be migration bug.

maria: agreed. I'll add reconcile + alerting to RFC. thanks everyone, i'll share draft in #architecture tomorrow and ping for review. :thumbsup:
